title: Communications outage
tldr: Conserve phone battery, try short texts for nonurgent check-ins and use a battery radio for official information. For immediate danger, try calling local emergency services; text-to-911 availability varies. Do not travel into danger just to find signal.
steps: Try a safe available landline, another carrier or Wi-Fi calling if configured and functioning.
Send your location, status and next check-in time to your out-of-area contact.
Lower brightness, enable low-power mode and limit unnecessary use.
If networks fail completely, follow the agreed safe meeting and contact arrangements.
next: Keep paper contact lists, offline maps and a radio. Arrange check-in times before a crisis.
watch: A message sent is not necessarily delivered. Do not assume emergency texting is supported everywhere.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: Write a short message with your status, location and next check-in time; try it periodically rather than draining the battery with constant retries. Use your agreed meeting plan only when the route is safe. Do not split up to hunt for signal.
household: Use one agreed check-in message and time so several people do not drain batteries repeating the same search. Share updates privately and include the time and location. Keep essential contacts on paper and teach children which trusted people they can approach.
pack_now: Keep essential medicines, drinking water, a battery light, shoes, phone power and a written contact card within reach. Adapt the load to the hazard and the people with you; do not delay escape to collect equipment.
